Sat 20:01 conversation at Whitfield house - kitchen with Jack Whitfield, Andrew Whitfield, Sophie Whitfield [ref 18:11]:
Jack Whitfield: "Smells brilliant, that. Right, I'll do the table in a sec, mum, honestly. Is it just the four of us, or is Sophie eating down here too? How long till it's ready, dad?" (Walks into the kitchen, grabs cutlery from the drawer and starts laying the table)
Julie Whitfield: "Oh hello love, you're just in time! Sophie's coming down, I think, I'll give her a shout in a minute. Dad's got the mince, so ten minutes or so, isn't it, Andrew? Jack, mind the good forks, they're in the left-hand drawer. Have you eaten anything today, bless you? You've got that look." (Stirs the veg pan, glances at the clock)
Sophie Whitfield: "Coming, mum. And yes, I've eaten, don't fuss. Toast, at some point." (comes in)
Jack Whitfield: "Yeah, I had a bit of a sandwich earlier, mum, honestly, I'm fine. Toast doesn't count though, Soph, to be fair. Right, forks, left-hand drawer, got them. Dad, is that shepherd's pie with the cheese on top? Please say cheese." (Keeps laying the table, putting out four sets of cutlery and the good forks)
Andrew Whitfield: "Cheese, yes, Jack, I'm not a monster. It's shepherd's pie, and it's got a bit of cheddar on top that I'll put under the grill for the last few minutes. Ten minutes or so, Julie's about right. Soph, toast does count as a food group in this house, but I'll make sure you get a decent portion of this as well." (Spoons the mince into the pie dish, tops the mash and scatters grated cheese over it)
Julie Whitfield: "Lovely, that's everyone then. Soph, love, sit yourself down by the radiator, you'll be warmer there. Jack, can you grab the gravy jug from the top cupboard and the water jug while you're up? I'll do the veg in a minute, the carrots are nearly there. Andrew, don't forget the grill, last time it caught and we had smoke everywhere!" (Drains the carrots and checks the peas, then wipes her hands on the tea towel)
Sophie Whitfield: "Fine, I'm sitting. Want me to do the water jug, Jack? I'm closer to the tap anyway." (sits by the radiator, then gets up again to fill the water jug)
Jack Whitfield: "Go on then, Soph, cheers. I'll get the gravy jug, top cupboard, yeah? Honestly, I always forget which one it is, it's the blue one, isn't it? Mum, do you want the veg dishes out as well?" (Finishes the last place setting, then reaches up into the top cupboard for the gravy jug)
Andrew Whitfield: "Jack, the gravy jug's the blue one, yes, though I'd check it's not the one with the chipped spout. Julie, the grill's on my list, I'm putting the pie under in a minute and I'll stand over it like a hawk. Veg dishes would be good, Jack, thanks." (Slides the pie dish under the grill and sets a timer on the cooker.)
Julie Whitfield: "Lovely, thanks both. Right, peas are done, so I'll get the veg into the dishes. Sophie, love, mind that jug, it's heavy when it's full, don't strain yourself. Jack, pop the dishes on the table when I've done them, and the mats are in the second drawer, I don't want the table marked." (Spoons carrots and peas into the veg dishes and wipes the edges with the tea towel)
Sophie Whitfield: "Jug's full. Mum, I've got it, it's not that heavy. Jack, can you grab the mats? I'll put it on the table." (Fills the water jug and carries it to the table, sits back down by the radiator.)
Jack Whitfield: "Mats, yeah, second drawer, on it. Honestly I'd forget my own head. Veg dishes too, mum, pass them over when they're done. Cheers for the jug, Soph." (Fetches the mats from the second drawer, puts them down and carries the veg dishes to the table)
Andrew Whitfield: "Right, that's about four minutes on the timer. Julie, I'm watching it, no smoke this time, I promise. Jack, is the blue jug the chipped one or not? Sophie, if you're sitting, you can pick the gravy. Granules or the proper stuff from the pan juices, I made a bit." (Stands by the grill, glancing at the timer, and wipes the worktop)
Julie Whitfield: "Proper gravy from the pan juices, Andrew, ooh lovely, Soph can you stir it for him? And Jack, it's the blue one, love, but the spout's only got a tiny chip, it won't hurt. Right, I'll bring the veg over. Have we got the sauce out for your dad? It's in the fridge door." (Carries the last of the veg dish to the table and fetches the sauce from the fridge door)
Sophie Whitfield: "Yeah, I'll stir it. Dad, is the pan juices thing already thickened or do you want me to put some flour in?" (Gets up from the radiator and goes over to the hob to stir the gravy.)
Andrew Whitfield: "Sophie, it's just the pan juices with a bit of cornflour in, so it's already near enough. Give it a stir and see. If it's too thin, a splash of the carrot water will do, but I'd leave it be. Jack, the blue jug's fine, a tiny chip never hurt anyone. Sauce on the table, lovely. Timer's nearly up, so everyone sit down and I'll bring this over." (Keeps an eye on the timer, then takes the pie out from under the grill with oven gloves.)
Jack Whitfield: "Sitting, sitting. Honestly that looks unreal, dad. Soph, how's the gravy, is it thick enough or are we having soup? Mum, you sit down as well, I'll grab the sauce and plates if we need them." (Pulls out a chair and sits at the table, pushing the sauce towards the middle)
Julie Whitfield: "Right, I'm sitting, I'm sitting! Ooh, that does look lovely, Andrew. Soph, is the gravy all right, love? Jack, plates are warming on the side there, would you mind? Then I'll get the serving spoon. Mind, it'll be hot, use the gloves!" (Puts the sauce down, sits at the table and rests her knee)
Sophie Whitfield: "Gravy's fine, dad, it's thick enough. Not soup. I'll bring it over." (Stirs the gravy, pours it into the blue jug and carries it to the table, then sits down.)
Andrew Whitfield: "Right, mind yourselves, it's hot. Jack, you're on plates, thanks. I'll serve it up, so pass them over one at a time. Cheese crust for whoever wants the corner, and I suspect I know who that is." (Carries the pie to the table, sets it on a mat and picks up the serving spoon.)
Jack Whitfield: "Go on then, plates, I'm on it. Honestly, dad, that corner is mine, you know me too well. Mum, you want a big bit or a small bit? Careful, Soph, it's boiling." (Gets up, takes the warm plates from the side using the oven gloves and passes them to Andrew one at a time)
Julie Whitfield: "Small bit for me, love, I'm not that hungry, bless you. Ooh, that smells lovely, Andrew. Jack, mind your sleeve on the gravy! Sophie, pass the sauce to your dad, would you? Right, everyone got a drink? Shall I pour the water?" (Holds her plate out to Andrew and reaches for the water jug)
Sophie Whitfield: "Yeah, I'll have water, thanks mum. Dad, just a normal bit for me, not a huge one. And Jack, you can have the corner, I'm not fighting you for it." (Passes the sauce across to Andrew and holds out her plate.)
Andrew Whitfield: "Here you go, Julie, small bit, with plenty of cheese on top. Jack, corner's yours, and mind the plate, it's hot. Soph, a normal bit, coming up. Right, sauce, thanks. Everyone dig in before it goes cold." (Serves the pie onto each plate in turn, passing them round, then sits down with his own.)
Jack Whitfield: "Mate, that corner is perfect, honestly. Cheers, dad. Mum, do you want the sauce or are you good? Soph, did you see the state of me with that oven glove, I nearly dropped the lot. Right, what are we watching after this, is it the reality stuff or the footy?" (Sits down with plate, digs into the cheesy corner)
